leads.title: Tennessee Supreme Court sets liquidated-damages standard for commercial PSAs — SH Nashville, LLC v. FWREF Nashville Airport, LLC
leads.why: Nov 16, 2026 Tennessee Supreme Court opinion (No. M2023-01147-SC-R11-CV) reversing the Court of Appeals and reinstating summary judgment for the seller of a Hilton-branded hotel near Nashville's airport, sold under a purchase and sale agreement. The court clarifies Tennessee's standard for enforcing a liquidated-damages clause versus treating it as an unenforceable penalty, holding a presumption of enforceability applies once the parties agreed actual damages would be hard to ascertain. Decided on the Davidson County Business Court docket; directly affects how CRE purchase agreements write and litigate liquidated-damages clauses statewide. Opinion itself is the primary source (full text in opinion-leads.json); background on the underlying hotel deal also appears in Tennessee court filings (tncourts.gov).

leads.title: Commonwealth Court affirms zoning board's denial of warehouse variance on former golf course — Water's Edge at Wind Gap, LLC v. ZHB of Moore Twp.
leads.why: Nov 16, 2026 Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court memorandum opinion (No. 279 C.D. 2024) affirming Northampton County's ruling that the Moore Township Zoning Hearing Board did not err in denying Water's Edge at Wind Gap, LLC a woodland-preservation variance needed for two warehouses (~488,000 sq ft) on the former Southmoore Golf Course. This is the third opinion in the case; secondary coverage (LehighValleyNews, PennFuture) explains the underlying industrial-warehouse zoning fight and the developer's planned Commonwealth Court appeal. Business entity (LLC developer) vs. township zoning board over industrial/warehouse site plan — squarely CRE development litigation.

leads.title: Ohio appeals court addresses regulatory-takings claim in county zoning enforcement suit — Dickard v. Jackson & Jackson, L.L.C.
leads.why: Nov 16, 2026 Ohio Twelfth District Court of Appeals opinion (2026-Ohio-4530) in a Butler County zoning inspector's injunctive-relief suit against Jackson & Jackson, LLC over an administrative office the LLC continued operating on its property after the county Board of Zoning Appeals denied a variance. The LLC counterclaimed alleging a regulatory taking; the appellate court's opinion addresses federal and state takings doctrine as applied to a commercial zoning-variance denial. No secondary press coverage found yet — this would run from the opinion itself (primary source) if the newsroom can verify no overlap with an already-tracked Butler County zoning matter.

leads.title: Minority investors sue to block Sachem Capital Corp.'s ~$2.9B reverse merger with Industrial Realty Group
leads.why: Sachem Capital Corp.'s Nov 16, 2026 Form 10-Q discloses that a complaint (filed July 27, 2026, Los Angeles Superior Court, Case No. 26STCV23391) by 17 minority investors in IRG Master Holdings now estimates damages at not less than $1.9 billion — the first time that figure has surfaced. The suit seeks to enjoin Sachem's planned reverse merger with Stuart Lichter's Industrial Realty Group, which would move nearly $3 billion of industrial real estate into a new public REIT (to be renamed IRG Realty Trust) and which a Los Angeles judge declined to halt on an emergency basis in July 2026 (Daily Journal). Not fresh (filed/ruled in July 2026) but significant and not currently tracked on the site; the $1.9B damages figure is newly disclosed this week. Event date given as the SEC disclosure date since that is what makes this newly reportable; the underlying filing date is 2026-07-27.
